hypothesis: One clean trial will produce all timing endpoints from monotonic timestamps and pass the existing public-caller, release, delayed-request-horizon, and fresh-session synthetic-task assertions.

decision.hold: environment unavailable before test entry, or raw/result cannot be retained
decision.pass: exit code 0; result JSON exists and has exactly one committed fresh-app event; required timing fields are finite/nonnegative; existing independent release/horizon/fresh-task assertions pass; runtime old cancellation remains UNKNOWN, release_confirmed=false, task_success=null, replay_allowed=false
decision.inference_limit: one synthetic Xvfb trial validates instrumentation and a bounded caller scenario only; it is not a reliability, efficiency, physical GUI, MAP01, or WSLc result

question: Does the corrected standard-caller Xvfb harness record distinct input-invocation-to-app-event, app-event-to-effect-commit, effect-commit-to-independent-readback, and caller cancellation invocation-to-return intervals while preserving existing cancellation and recovery assertions?

inputs.task: existing synthetic Xvfb held-key cancellation followed by one fresh-session key-c effect
inputs.application_effect: synthetic app property committed after app_display.sync()

design.arm: prestarted supervisor enabled; server pause disabled; zero cancel-ack hold
design.stopping: first run is terminal whether PASS, FAIL, HOLD, timeout, or missing receipt

allocation.network: only dependency install if the pinned packages are absent; no network during the trial

frozen_environment.storage: repository packet under /mnt/c; temporary harness directory uses WSL /tmp
